innate.name: Making and speaking first
innate.behavior: In a meeting where the problem is still being described, you are already sketching the fix on the whiteboard or saying the blunt version out loud. You draft the email before the requirements are finalized, you build the rough prototype before the budget is approved, and you give the honest opinion before someone asks for it. The output is not polished — it is a working version that lets everyone else react to something concrete instead of a discussion. You feel more alive after a session where you produced a draft, a fix, or a straight answer than after a day of listening and planning.
innate.evidence: Eating God is the leading force and jointly heaviest with Companion (9 and 8). The month stem is Eating God, the day branch is Eating God, and the year branch hidden stems include Eating God. The Day Master is slightly strong (偏旺), so output is a favorable direction — producing drains the excess rather than depleting you.

innate.name: Steadying with what you already know
innate.behavior: When the first draft gets pushback, you do not panic — you reach for a framework, a past case, or a credential you already hold and use it to anchor the next version. You say 'we solved something like this before' and pull up the old document. You cite a standard or a certification to end a debate. You keep a personal library of notes, templates, and precedents, and you return to it when the output runs into a wall. The base is what lets you produce again without starting from zero.
innate.evidence: Direct Resource weighs 6, carried by the month and hour branch hidden stems (both 巳 hold 正印). The Day Master is slightly strong, so Resource adds weight rather than relieving it — it functions as a store you draw on, not a source that overwhelms you.

innate.name: Moving with peers who act
innate.behavior: You do your best work next to someone who is also building. You pair on a task, split the work, and check in at short intervals. When a project stalls, you call the one colleague who will actually do something rather than the one who will only discuss it. You are comfortable being the first to move if someone is moving with you, and you lose momentum when you are the only one pushing. The Companion energy shows up as co-production, not solo grinding.
innate.evidence: Companion is jointly heaviest with Eating God (8). The hour stem is Companion, and the year branch hidden stems include Companion. The Day Master is slightly strong, so Companion is not a lifeline you lack — it is a natural mode of working alongside others.

trained.name: Securing backing before you act
trained.behavior: Before you commit to a big output, you check whether you have the credential, the approval, or the institutional cover. You ask 'who signed off on this?' before you start. You keep your certifications current and your references warm. You prefer to produce inside a structure that will back you rather than as a free agent. This shows up as a pause before the first draft — a quick scan for whether the ground is solid — and it makes your output look more deliberate than it feels from the inside.
trained.trained_by: Direct Resource at 6 is the second-strongest force after the output axis, and the Day Master is slightly strong — the environment rewarded having a base before producing. Early on, producing without backing likely met resistance, so you learned to secure the base first. The cost is speed: the pause before the first draft can turn into a delay, and you may wait for approval that is not coming.
trained.evidence: Direct Resource weighs 6, carried by the month and hour branch hidden stems. The Day Master is slightly strong (偏旺), so Resource is a weight you carry rather than a deficiency you fill — it was added by environment, not given by the structure's leading force.

trained.name: Reading the room before speaking
trained.behavior: You have a blunt opinion ready, but you check who is in the room and what the power map is before you say it. You soften the first sentence, then land the point. You notice when the honest version will cost you and you choose the timing. This is not dishonesty — it is a trained filter between the Eating God output and the Seven Killings edge. The behavior is visible as a half-second pause before the direct statement, and as a follow-up message that says the sharper thing in writing rather than in the meeting.
trained.trained_by: Seven Killings weighs 5 and sits in the year stem (乙), the earliest position — pressure from authority or a demanding early environment. The blunt output of Eating God met that pressure, and you learned to filter before speaking. The long-term cost is that the filter can become a habit even when the room is safe, so the direct version arrives later than it needs to.
trained.evidence: Seven Killings weighs 5, carried by the year stem. Eating God is the leading force at 9. The Day Master is slightly strong, so the Killings are a pressure to manage rather than a threat to survival — the filter is a trained response, not a structural necessity.

defensive.name: Waiting for the base to be perfect
defensive.looks_like: Preparation, diligence, and high standards. Outsiders see someone who does the reading before the meeting, who has the documentation ready, who does not ship something half-baked. It looks like professionalism.
defensive.actual_cost: It drains you because the base is already sufficient — Direct Resource at 6 is a store, not a shortage — and the waiting is a trained reflex, not a real requirement. You spend energy topping up a base that would carry the output now, and the output gets delayed or narrowed. The cost shows up as a draft that sits finished in a folder while you check one more source, and as a range of work that stops widening because the new input never gets used.
defensive.evidence: Direct Resource weighs 6 and the Day Master is slightly strong (偏旺), so Resource is a weight, not a lifeline. The core loop leaks when the base is drawn on without being topped up — but the defensive version is the opposite error: topping up without drawing. The Bing Zi luck pillar starting around age 42 brings water into the branch, which makes new input easier to absorb; the defensive pattern is the habit that resists it.

defensive.name: Filtering the blunt version until it is safe
defensive.looks_like: Tact, diplomacy, and reading the room. Outsiders see someone who does not burn bridges and who lands the point without collateral damage. It looks like maturity.
defensive.actual_cost: It drains you because the Eating God output is the leading force and the natural mode is to say the thing — the filter is a trained layer on top, and running it costs energy every time. The cost shows up as a meeting where you said the softened version and then spent the evening drafting the sharp one, and as a reputation for being less direct than you actually are. The output still happens, but it happens later and in a lower-energy channel.
defensive.evidence: Eating God is the leading force at 9, and the Day Master is slightly strong, so output is the favorable direction. Seven Killings weighs 5 in the year stem — the earliest position — which is where the filter was trained. The defensive cost is the gap between the Eating God output and the Seven Killings filter.

one_leverage: Keep the first ability — making and speaking first — as your lever. It is the leading force of the chart (Eating God at 9, jointly heaviest with Companion at 8), it is the direction the slightly strong Day Master favors, and it is the one ability that gains energy while you use it. The other two innate abilities support it: the base gives the output something to draw on, and the peers give it momentum. The trained and defensive patterns are filters and delays around this lever, not replacements for it. If you keep only one, keep the one that produces the draft, the fix, or the straight answer before the room is ready — and use the base and the peers to make that output land, not to postpone it.
